conviction_note: The largest piece of the print, BioMar's Q3 (EBIT DKK 618m vs 411m) and its FY EBIT raise (+DKK 75m at midpoint), was public from 2 Nov 15:40 CET. Schouw itself said that day it would revisit its group guide by 6 Nov, so a guidance raise is near-certain but its BioMar part is priced. What is still unknown is how much the other five businesses add and what cash flow looks like. abs_move 5.5 is set on the name's own observed report-day moves (median about 5%, max 10%) plus a near-certain guidance change. p_up 54 is a slight lean: upgrade momentum after +32% over 60d on one side; the subsidiary selling its own raise, the stock at the sell-side average target and weak H1 cash on the other. The findings sum (+0.10) and the scaled number (+0.44) agree in sign and are both small.

already_public.what: BioMar (fully consolidated) Q3 2026: revenue DKK 5,807m (+19%), EBIT DKK 618m vs 411m; YTD EBIT 977m

BioMar FY2026 guide raised: revenue DKK 17.8-18.6bn (from 17-18bn), EBIT DKK 1,290-1,360m (from 1,200-1,300m); volume cut to 1,600-1,650kt; Schouw says it will update its group guide no later than the 6 Nov Q3 report
Group FY2026 guide: EBITDA DKK 3,150-3,350m (raised 14 Aug), revenue DKK 35.1-37.6bn after the Spectre closing (EBITDA unchanged)
Capital Markets Day: 2030 EBITDA ambition DKK 4.5bn, leverage target 1.0-2.5x, dividend policy reiterated

new_in_release.expect: Group EBITDA guide raised. The BioMar-mechanical +DKK 75m (to about 3,225-3,425m) is public; the upside is a further raise from HydraSpecma, Fibertex PC, Fibertex NW, Borg or GPV. Direction up, size beyond BioMar unknown
Q3 group EBITDA well above the 878m of Q3 2025, inferred at about DKK 1.1-1.16bn, mostly from BioMar's already-public +207m EBIT. Up, but mostly known
Risk line: H1 operating cash flow was 436m vs 762m, and BioMar's raw-material-driven revenue growth points to a working-capital build. Direction unknown, leaning weak
Q4 commentary: BioMar flagged a softer Q4 on volumes; for the rest of the group, unknown
Possible buyback extension or update, given NIBD/EBITDA of 0.7x against the 1.0-2.5x target. Unknown

session_check: bmo. No release time has been published for 6 Nov itself; the verdict rests on the issuer's unbroken pattern. Q2 2026 went out 08:01-08:02 CEST (https://view.news.eu.nasdaq.com/view?id=b44bbbdbe1608c1cc3ae4661c0e1343cc&lang=en&src=listed), Q1 2026 at 08:00 CEST, FY2025 at 08:02 CET and Q3 2025 at 08:00 CET (https://www.inderes.dk/releases/interim-report-third-quarter-of-2025), all before the 09:00 Copenhagen open. The date 6 Nov is confirmed by the issuer's 2026 financial calendar (https://www.inderes.fi/releases/schouw-and-cos-financial-calendar-2026) and restated in its 2 Nov announcement ('Q3 interim report scheduled on 6 November 2026').
positioning_check: Finanstilsynet aggregated net short register (0.1% threshold), fetched 2026-11-05 with entries timestamped that day (https://www.dfsa.dk/financial-themes/capital-market/company-announcements/aggregated-net-short-positions). 47 issuers listed, the lowest at 0.10%. Neither Schouw (ISIN DK0010253921) nor BioMar appears. So no disclosed net short of 0.1% or more: a real near-zero, checked by ISIN and not only by name. No squeeze fuel, and building or covering cannot be measured from a snapshot.

findings.finding: BioMar's 2 Nov release, already public, puts Schouw's group guide up mechanically by about DKK 75m of EBITDA at midpoint (BioMar EBIT 1,290-1,360m vs 1,200-1,300m) and lifts Q3 group EBITDA by about +207m y/y from BioMar alone (EBIT 618m vs 411m); Schouw committed to incorporate it by 6 Nov.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Group guide raises were rewarded: Q2 2026 (14 Aug) raise +6.75% on the day and +5.29% the next; Q1 2026 +4.11%. Q3 2025's narrowing to the low end: -1.32%. BioMar's own raises have been public before Schouw's (12 Aug, then 14 Aug).
findings.original_quote: Schouw & Co. ... vil vurdere sine samlede forventninger ... senest i forbindelse med offentliggørelsen af delårsrapporten for 3. kvartal den 6. november 2026 (Danish version via https://via.ritzau.dk/pressemeddelelse/15265541/aktieselskabet-schouw-and-co?publisherId=90446; English: 'will consider its consolidated full-year guidance ... no later than in connection with the release of the Q3 interim report scheduled on 6 November 2026')
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: published inside the 2 Nov session, with three sessions since; Schouw closed 828 -> 843 (+1.8%). What is not priced is only the exact form the group guide takes; if the market had fully priced a large group raise, the stock would have broken above its 21 Oct high of 850, and it has not.
findings.independence: Same document family as the BioMar Q3 report (https://view.news.eu.nasdaq.com/view?id=b5656ebb2ebc4c36ff7e3a1d3003bdc14&lang=en&src=listed); one fact, merged here.

findings.finding: BioMar's own shares sold its raise: -3.3% on 2 Nov and -2.9% on 3 Nov (129.8 -> 121.7 by 5 Nov), after BioMar said Q3 profitability came from 'temporary market conditions ... not necessarily expected to persist' and cut volume guidance for a 'softer last quarter'. The quality of the largest contributor to Schouw's raise is doubted, and Schouw's look-through value fell with it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: First quarter in which BioMar, listed since May 2026, sold its own raise; on 12 Aug BioMar +2.1% and Schouw +6.75% two days later.
findings.why_not_priced: BioMar has repriced, but Schouw rose over the same three sessions, so the market treats Schouw as if the BioMar raise were clean. If Schouw's Q3 commentary echoes the 'temporary' framing, the parent can catch down; if the parent had already absorbed it, it would have fallen with BioMar on 2-3 Nov.

findings.finding: Implied-Q4 arithmetic leaves room for a raise beyond BioMar. H1 EBITDA was 1,419m; Q3 is inferred at about 1.1-1.16bn. A guide raised only by BioMar's +75m (midpoint about 3,325m) would imply Q4 2026 EBITDA of about 610-680m, below Q4 2025's 731m, which itself carried part of 'almost DKK 100 million' of 2025 restructuring costs. The other five businesses were all raised or held at Q2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: At Q2 the raise beyond BioMar (HydraSpecma, Fibertex PC and NW, Borg) produced a +6.75% day; at Q3 2025 a narrowing to the low end produced -1.32%.
findings.why_not_priced: It is an inference, and with no Q3 consensus anywhere the market has no published anchor for the non-BioMar half. If a larger raise were expected, the stock would have reacted on 2 Nov when the BioMar number arrived, not sat flat at 828.
findings.independence: Q3/Q4 2025 group figures (EBITDA 878 and 731) from https://www.inderes.fi/en/companies/Schouw-and-Co/financials-and-estimates/quarter-data; 2025 restructuring costs from https://www.inderes.fi/releases/interim-report-third-quarter-of-2025

findings.finding: Nordic EMS peers printed strong Q3 2026 (Scanfil organic growth about 8.5% per a Nordea note, 2-3% above consensus), a positive read-through for GPV, which carries about 22% of the group EBITDA guide (710-750m) and had flat Q2 revenue on component constraints.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: GPV has not been the swing line in the recent reactions; its Q2 guide was narrowed, not raised.
findings.why_not_priced: A peer proxy; the GPV-specific number is unseen. Small because GPV's constraint was component supply, not demand, and a proxy is not the company.

findings.finding: The stock goes into the print at the sell-side average target (about DKK 852 across 3 analysts, high 880, against spot 843) after +32% in 60 sessions, with no disclosed short to squeeze, so upside on a pre-signalled raise is limited unless targets move.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: After Q2 the stock ran from 637 to 771 within two weeks, so targets have lagged the price before without stopping it.
findings.source_date: 2026-11-05 (snippet_only; page returned no body to curl)
findings.original_quote: genomsnitt 851,7 baserat på tre analytiker, högsta 880, lägsta 820 (snippet)
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced by definition; it bears on the reaction, not the number. Sized small and snippet-based.

findings.finding: Weak cash flow is a risk line: H1 2026 operating cash flow was DKK 436m vs 762m (Q2 410m vs 542m, -24%), and BioMar's Q3 revenue growth was driven by higher raw-material prices, which points to a working-capital build in Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 cash-flow decline was overlooked on a guide-raise day (+6.75%).
findings.why_not_priced: The Q3 cash number is unseen. Offsetting it, BioMar's own NIBD/EBITDA improved to 1.37x from 1.45x in Q3, so the build may be modest.
findings.independence: BioMar Q3 raw-material commentary and leverage, https://view.news.eu.nasdaq.com/view?id=b5656ebb2ebc4c36ff7e3a1d3003bdc14&lang=en&src=listed

findings.finding: Balance-sheet capacity for capital return: NIBD/EBITDA was 0.7x at Q2 against a reconfirmed 1.0-2.5x target, the buyback was increased by up to DKK 170m on 14 Aug and runs weekly, and treasury shares already exceed 10%; an extension or a new programme could come with Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 14 Aug buyback increase came on the same day as the guide raise; its separate effect is not identifiable.
findings.why_not_priced: Speculative timing: no statement says a new programme comes on 6 Nov. Spectre (closed 1 Sep) consumed part of the capacity.

lessons_applied: 'The move is in the guide' (guidance change median 9.0%): abs_move_pct raised from 4.5 to 5.5, since a group guide change is near-certain, held below 9 because the BioMar part is pre-released.
'A finding about a number the market has already been told is worth 0': the BioMar-mechanical guidance finding cut from +0.4 to +0.2.
'Cash can outweigh a raised guide' (Luceco): filed the H1 operating-cash-flow decline as its own finding (-0.3); it had been found in the Q2 report but left unfiled in the draft.
'A beat made of a one-off is sold' (H&M): supports the BioMar 'temporary conditions' finding at -0.4 unchanged, and moved p_up from 55 to 54.
